# C-1 · System Description

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Step | C Categorize (system level) |
| Phases | PH-MSA (primary), PH-TMRR |
| Depends on | P-15, P-18 |
| Inputs | ART-BND, ART-REQ, ART-INV, EXT-PRODUCT |
| Outputs | ART-SD (produces), ART-BND (updates) |
| Writes facts | system_id, system_name, acronym, aliases, lifecycle_state, classification, system_type, owning_organization, system_version, operational_environment, lifecycle_phase |
| Minimum interviews | 1 |
| RACI | R: PER-PM, PER-ISSM · A: PER-PM · C: PER-AO, PER-IO, PER-PRIV, PER-LSE · I: — · PER-PRIV only when the system processes PII |
| Persona cards | [PER-PM](../../personas/PER-PM.md), [PER-ISSM](../../personas/PER-ISSM.md), [PER-AO](../../personas/PER-AO.md), [PER-IO](../../personas/PER-IO.md), [PER-PRIV](../../personas/PER-PRIV.md), [PER-LSE](../../personas/PER-LSE.md) |

Purpose: Document the characteristics of the system, its users and the authorizations it leverages; the PM provides the system description.
<!-- END rmf:header -->
<!-- rmf:body authored -->

## Steps

1. **Entry check.** `uv run rmf status <run>` names C-1; `artifacts/ART-BND.md`,
   `artifacts/ART-INV.md` and `artifacts/ART-REQ.md` exist (P-15 and P-18 are done,
   deferred or seeded). Why: the description builds on the boundary, inventory and
   requirements.
2. **Read the inputs** in `## Inputs`.
3. **Interview** PER-PM, then PER-IO (`## Interviews`). The PM provides the system
   description (DoDI 8510.01 §4.4.b(5)(i)); the IO describes the user community and how its
   information is used.
4. **Write the identity facts.** Rewrite `facts.yaml` whole, keeping every existing field,
   and set `system_id`, `system_name`, `acronym`, `aliases` and `lifecycle_state`, each with
   `set_by_task: C-1` and `sources`:

   ```yaml
   system_name:
     value: "Example Sensor Gateway"
     set_by_task: C-1
     sources: [INT-004.A1, product/profile.yaml]
   acronym:
     value: "ESG"
     set_by_task: C-1
     sources: [INT-004.A1]
   aliases:
     value: []
     set_by_task: C-1
     sources: [INT-004.A1]
   system_id:
     value: "ESG-001"
     set_by_task: C-1
     sources: [ASM-001]
   lifecycle_state:
     value: under-development
     set_by_task: C-1
     sources: [product/conops.md#program]
   ```

   - `system_name` and `acronym`: the PM's confirmation of the proposed values in
     `product/profile.yaml` (proposed values are never facts until a task confirms them).
   - `system_id`: the identifier from system registration (P-18). If neither ART-REG nor
     the product gives one, record an assumption (`ASM-###`, persona PER-PM) that the
     identifier is `<ACRONYM>-001` until registration assigns one, and cite it.
   - `lifecycle_state`: an OSCAL value: `operational`, `under-development`,
     `under-major-modification`, `disposition`, `other`.
   - Why: FACTS-001 requires each field with `set_by_task: C-1`, and every artifact and the
     OSCAL SSP take identity from here (INV-4).
   Then set the system facts beside identity, each with `set_by_task: C-1` and `sources`
   (SYSD-001; the facts block of every core document shows them, CNSSI 1254 Annex C):
   - `classification`: `value` (`unclassified`, `confidential`, `secret`, `top-secret`, the
     highest level of information the system stores, processes or transmits), `compartments`
     (`sci`, `sap`, `aea`) and `handling_markings` (dissemination controls such as `CUI` or
     `NOFORN`). Work the level out with the security classification guide's authority
     (DoDI 5000.83). A level above unclassified means C-2 applies the Classified System
     Overlay; unclassified means it does not.
   - `system_type`: `value` (`enclave`, `major-application`, `pit-system`,
     `general-support-system`), `connectivity` (`stand-alone`, `networked`),
     `dodin_connection` (`direct`, `indirect`, `none`) and `rationale`. An enclave lists the
     systems it `hosts` with their C/I/A: it is categorized no lower than any of them. A PIT
     system records `designated_by` (`osd-component-head`, `dod-component-head`, `delegate`),
     `registered_in` (the Component register) and `pit_ao_appointed: true`.
   - `owning_organization`, `system_version` (`value`, `release_date`),
     `operational_environment` (`production`, `test`, `research-and-development`, `tactical`,
     `deployed`, `other`) and `lifecycle_phase` (`PH-MSA` ... `PH-OS`, CNSSI 1254's numbered
     phase).
   Why: these are system facts (INV-4); the classification sets the handling marking of the
   documents that hold vulnerability or configuration detail (SYSD-006).
5. **Write `artifacts/data/system-description.yaml`** from
   `templates/data/system-description.yaml`: `ownership`, the `function` narrative, the
   `physical_environment` (building, walls and ceilings, physical security, TEMPEST or SCIF
   validation), the `service_alignment` (NOSC, GENSER or SE designation, the CSSP agreement
   `SVA-###` of `service-agreements.yaml`, who authorized the CSSP: CDRUSSTRATCOM or
   USCYBERCOM for GENSER, DIA for SE; the register, mission criticality, IP ranges and
   locations), and one `interconnections` record per boundary component of type
   `interconnection` with its interface, agreement, signatories and the other system's
   authorization. A mission partner agreement states the DODIN operations responsibilities,
   the cybersecurity requirements, the protection of DoD data and the incident reporting
   contacts, and is based on the Component risk assessment, DoD risk tolerance guidance and
   interconnection policy; a foreign partner's is an international agreement, a Defense
   contractor's a contract, and a federal partner subscribes to a DoD CSSP or holds an
   equivalent capability (DoDI 8530.01 Encl 4, SYSD-002, SYSD-003). M-1 records a CSSP
   change under `service_alignment.changes` with whom it was reported to.
6. **Write `artifacts/data/users.yaml`** from `templates/data/users.yaml`: one record per user
   group (`USR-<NAME>`), with `type`, `privilege_level` (`privileged`, `non-privileged`,
   `no-logical-access`), `category` (CNSSI 1254's user categories), `access_requirements`
   (clearance, compartments, citizenship), `roles`, `authorized_privileges` (each with
   `functions_performed`) and `sources`. A privileged group records `privileged_access`:
   its members are qualified and have signed a Statement of Acceptance of Responsibilities.
   A foreign-national or coalition-partner group records `foreign_access`: access authorized
   by the DoD Component head, the disclosure guidance, and what limits access to
   information cleared for release (DoDI 8500.01, SYSD-004). Include groups with no logical access when the
   system serves them (for example people who only see its outputs elsewhere).
   Each group records `access_decision` (the system owner, with the information owner; not
   for `no-logical-access`) and `training` (the system owner; not for `general-public`)
   (ASMT-013). Why: the system owner answers for who gets in and what they were taught.
7. **Write `artifacts/data/leveraged-authorizations.yaml`** from
   `templates/data/leveraged-authorizations.yaml`: one `LA-##` record per separately
   authorized provider whose controls the system inherits, with `provider`,
   `date_authorized`, `decision` (`AD-ATO`, ...), the `service` consumed and its agreement
   (an internal DoD service under an SLA; an external one under an interagency agreement,
   statement of work or contract incorporating the DoDI 8500.01 security requirements;
   `enterprise` when it is an enterprise-level agreement, used when possible; SYSD-005) and
   `sources`. An interconnected system the
   system only exchanges data with is not a leveraged authorization. If there are none,
   write `leveraged_authorizations: []`. Set `arrangement` on each record: a
   `common-control-provider` must be the provider of a common control in `allocation.yaml`; an
   `organizational-system` names its authorizing `decision`, its
   `authorization_termination_date` and `ao_aware`, because this system's AO is told of the
   inheritance (MLEV-001).
8. **Update the boundary.** Rewrite `artifacts/data/boundary.yaml` whole, setting
   `leveraged_authorization: LA-##` on each external component covered by a leveraged
   authorization and correcting anything the interviews changed. Then append `C-1` to
   `touched_by` in `artifacts/ART-BND.md` (and add a traced sentence for any change). Why:
   C-1 lists ART-BND as an output, and the task is not done until ART-BND's `touched_by`
   includes C-1.
9. **Write `artifacts/ART-SD.md`** from `templates/artifacts/ART-SD.md`: mission and
   purpose, system description and functions, users and their access, operating
   environment, interconnections and leveraged authorizations; every section traced. Refer
   to the system by role ("the system"), not by restating the name or ID; `rmf build`
   injects the facts block.
   **Reciprocity.** Write `artifacts/data/reciprocity.yaml` from `templates/data/reciprocity.yaml` (ART-SD keeps it
   from here to M-7): `receiving_organizations` for each organization this system is deployed
   into, `received_systems` for each system deployed into this one, `[]` for a side it does
   not have. An ATO at enterprise scope needs a Receiving organization (RCP-001); an
   Enterprise system received in `leveraged-authorizations.yaml` needs a received system
   (RCP-004), unless it is used in its native environment only (`co_use` with its
   notification processes). Each Receiving organization records when it `joined`. Each
   relationship rests on an executed documented agreement (such as an MOU, MOA, SLA or ISA) in `agreements`
   with the minimum topics, package-sharing terms, this side's single POC (a role of the
   run), a technical POC on each side, notification processes, timing, requirements and
   recipients (`pm`, `original-ao`), termination factors of an MOU or MOA, the pre-agreement
   tasks with their responsible organization, deviations accepted by both sides and the core
   documents agreed; a software factory's agreement also passes software across and feedback
   back (RCP-006). A received system is accepted only after its agreement is executed.

10. **Build and check.** `uv run rmf build <run>`, then `uv run rmf check <run> --task C-1`,
   until 0 errors. INV-BND-001 starts to apply here: every inventory item's component must
   be a boundary component.
11. **Journal** a CHECKPOINT.

## Interviews

| Persona | Why | Question focus |
|---|---|---|
| PER-PM | accountable (A); provides the system description | official name and acronym, registry identifier, lifecycle state, mission and functions, sites and quantities, interconnections and agreements |
| PER-IO | consulted (C); speaks for the information and its users | who uses the system's outputs, user groups and their privileges, how information leaves the system |
| PER-ISSM (optional) | responsible (R) | leveraged authorizations and their dates, privileged roles |

At least 1 interview; this playbook expects the PER-PM and PER-IO interviews.

## Inputs

- `artifacts/ART-BND.md`, `artifacts/data/boundary.yaml`
- `artifacts/ART-INV.md`, `artifacts/data/inventory.yaml`
- `artifacts/ART-REQ.md`
- `product/conops.md`, `product/profile.yaml`, `product/architecture.md`

| File | Front-matter | Notes |

| `artifacts/data/users.yaml` | — | schema `users` |
| `artifacts/data/leveraged-authorizations.yaml` | — | schema `leveraged-authorizations` |

## Facts

| Field | Source |
|---|---|
| `system_name`, `acronym`, `aliases` | the PM's confirmation of `product/profile.yaml` |
| `system_id` | registration (ART-REG) or an assumption |
| `lifecycle_state` | the PM's answer or the product's lifecycle statement |
| `classification`, `system_type`, `owning_organization`, `system_version`, `operational_environment`, `lifecycle_phase` | the PM's answers, the classification guide and the product |

## Done when

- ART-SD, `users.yaml` and `leveraged-authorizations.yaml` describe the system.
- `facts.yaml` has `system_id`, `system_name`, `acronym`, `aliases` and `lifecycle_state`,
  each with `set_by_task: C-1`.
- ART-BND lists C-1 in `touched_by`.
- `uv run rmf check <run> --task C-1` reports 0 errors.

## Journal and lessons

- CHECKPOINT: `## <time> · CHECKPOINT · task C-1`, naming the facts set and any assumption
  recorded.
- If the PM changed a proposed value from `product/profile.yaml`, say which in the
  CHECKPOINT body.
